theme: Population, migration and second-home data (IRS migration, Census CPS, USPS change of address, second-home counts, holiday-home shares Europe)

candidates.name: IRS-migration-data (mathewhauer)
candidates.what_it_holds: R scripts that download and process raw IRS Statistics-of-Income migration files into one flat file `county_migration_data.txt` covering 1990-2010, 95-98% of the tax-filing universe; 5-digit FIPS origin county, 2-digit FIPS destination state, flows under 10 filers coded 99999. Includes manuscript/LaTeX explaining methodology. 22 stars, MIT code / CC-BY-3.0 data, last commit 2024-05-23.
candidates.why_useful: Long-run, cleanly documented county-level migration series (sunbelt in-migration, second-home-market feeder counties) that is a candidate proxy for where new short-term-rental demand/supply and vacation-home purchases concentrate; gap 20 (geotagged tourism/migration proxies) and general population-shift context for NA nights.
candidates.size_hint: single flat file + ~2000 legacy source files processed

candidates.name: Hurricanes_and_Migration
candidates.what_it_holds: Complete county-to-county migration flow matrices built from IRS-SOI data, 1998-2015, as CSVs in outflows/ and inflows/ folders (yearly matrices e.g. 0101in.csv, plus aggregated outflow.csv/inflow.csv). Also ships hurricanes.json: US federal disaster assistance records 1990-2018 with affected county FIPS, costs, casualties, dates. Python scripts analyze migration response to Katrina and Sandy.
candidates.why_useful: Longer span than the mathewhauer repo (through 2015) and pairs migration directly with hurricane/disaster shocks by county — directly useful for gap 11 (events/shocks, hurricanes) and for modeling population/second-home exposure to storm-affected STR markets (Florida, Gulf Coast, coastal Northeast).
candidates.size_hint: per-year CSV matrices, dozens of files

candidates.name: migration-flow-tool
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool for building county-to-county migration patterns from IRS tax data; updated 2026-08-06 (recent/active).
candidates.why_useful: A currently-maintained (2026) method for pulling/refreshing IRS migration data, useful if the team wants a live-updating migration feed rather than a frozen historical dump.

candidates.name: county-migration
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool to look up where people moved from/to for any US county using IRS SOI county-to-county migration flow data; MIT licensed, updated 2026-08-13 (recent).
candidates.why_useful: Another actively maintained IRS-SOI migration lookup tool; corroborates data availability and gives a second, recent implementation to cross-check against mathewhauer's historical build.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps mathewhauer/IRS-migration-data and eugeniopaglino/Hurricanes_and_Migration in source data, different implementation

candidates.name: population-demographics-de-project
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-engineering pipeline and interactive mapping tool combining Census ACS, TIGER/Line geographies, and IRS migration data 2012-2024 at state/county/tract granularity; updated 2026-08-21 (recent, wide time span through 2024).
candidates.why_useful: Widest and most recent time span (2012-2024) of any migration repo found here; a maintained pipeline that could be re-run to get current-vintage IRS migration + ACS demographic joins for identifying growing STR/second-home markets.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline + generated outputs, not fully inspected

candidates.name: IRS-Migration-Outflow
candidates.what_it_holds: Code that converts raw IRS migration files into a unified county-to-county outflow dataset; updated 2025-12-06.
candidates.why_useful: Another recent (Dec 2025) IRS migration outflow builder; minor incremental value over the other IRS repos already listed.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps other IRS-SOI migration repos above

candidates.name: ResSecFrance2015 (Les résidences secondaires en France en 2015)
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-year (2015) French second-home (résidence secondaire) dataset by geography, per repo title; not further verified beyond listing metadata.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme (European second-home/holiday-home counts) though only one year and one country; could anchor a France-specific holiday-home base rate if verified.

candidates.name: global-emigration-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 9 CSVs from WhereToEmigrate covering 2,500+ visa/residency pathways across 190+ countries: easiest-countries ranking, digital-nomad-visa income thresholds and PR routes, processing times, immigration pathways by category, income/savings thresholds, cost-of-living by country, salary-by-profession, quality-of-life indices, plus a data dictionary. CC BY 4.0, snapshot July 2026, refreshed quarterly by the source.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap 16 (remote-work/long-stay demand, digital-nomad visa datasets) with a structured, country-level digital-nomad-visa panel that could proxy long-stay demand growth markets for Airbnb.

candidates.name: Digital-Nomad-Research
candidates.what_it_holds: Human-verified 33-jurisdiction digital-nomad-visa policy dataset plus a 190-country macroeconomic panel, with a reproducible validation workflow and downstream TWFE / Callaway-Santa'Anna difference-in-differences evaluation code; MIT licensed, updated 2026-08-22.
candidates.why_useful: A research-grade (causal-inference-ready) digital-nomad-visa panel — complements the 0brien18 dataset above for gap 16, and the DiD code itself is a reusable method for event-study style analysis of policy shocks (also relevant to gap 12 STR-regulation event studies methodologically).
candidates.size_hint: policy dataset + macro panel + code, not fully inspected

notes: WebSearch tool's shared session budget (200/200) was exhausted before any query for this theme ran, so this scout relied entirely on gh search repos plus targeted WebFetch verification, per the modality fallback instructions. DuckDB html endpoint refused connections outright (ECONNREFUSED); Bing's page did return but did not surface github.com results for these queries even with site:github.com, so it was abandoned after two tries. github.com/search (the web UI) 429'd for an hour after two calls, so it could not be used either. No USPS change-of-address, no Census CPS geographic-mobility microdata repo, and no European holiday-home/second-home share dataset (beyond one thin single-year French repo) were found on GitHub — this looks like a genuine gap: USPS COA data is proprietary/paid (not freely redistributable), CPS geographic mobility tables live at census.gov but nobody has mirrored them as a repo, and Eurostat holds a `hbs` or tourism second-home series but no GitHub mirror surfaced. The IRS county-migration space is well covered by multiple repos (several actively updated in 2025-2026), all built on the same underlying IRS-SOI source, so treat the four IRS repos here as one data source with several independent tools rather than four distinct datasets. The digital-nomad-visa datasets are the most novel find relative to what CONTEXT.md says we hold, directly addressing gap 16. Recommend a follow-up scout with a fresh WebSearch budget specifically for 'USPS ADS-2 change of address' aggregate/county-level public data and 'Eurostat second home' / 'holiday home Europe Airbnb' since gh search text-matching under-serves phrase queries with special characters or non-English terms.
